basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '(Cap. III.—Vers. 1.) Serpens autem erat sapientior cunctis bestiis super terram. Pro'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. III.—Vers. 1.) Serpens autem erat sapientior cunctis bestiis super terram. Pro sapiente in Hebraeo habetur AROM (ערום), quod Aquila et Theodotion πανοῦργον interpretati sunt: hoc est, nequam et versipellem. Magis itaque ex hoc verbo calliditas et versutia, quam sapientia demonstratur.
